subject: Mathematics

outcomes.text: Recall that a complex number is written a + ib, or as the pair (a, b), with i the square root of minus one.
Name the real part and the imaginary part of a complex number.
State when two complex numbers are equal.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers.
Define the conjugate of a complex number as a - ib.
Define and find the modulus of a complex number, the square root of a squared plus b squared.
Solve a pair of linear equations whose coefficients are complex numbers.
Write a polynomial as a product of linear factors using complex roots.
Solve a quadratic with real coefficients over the complex numbers by completing the square.
Explain how the polar coordinate system locates a point.
Write a complex number in polar form with modulus and argument.
Multiply, divide and take powers of complex numbers in polar form.
Handle simple equations and inequalities with complex numbers in polar form.
Use complex numbers on real problems such as cryptography, waves, circuits and fluid flow.
Add, subtract and multiply matrices with real or complex entries.
Find a 3 by 3 determinant using cofactors and the properties of determinants.

subtopics.title: Inverse and rank of a matrix

outcomes.text: Use row operations to find the inverse and the rank of a matrix.
Explain consistent and inconsistent linear systems with examples.
Solve a 3 by 3 non-homogeneous system by matrix inverse and by Cramer's rule.
Solve three homogeneous equations in three unknowns by Gaussian elimination.
Apply matrices to problems such as graphics, encryption, seismic analysis and networks.
Solve problems on arithmetic sequences and series up to n terms.
Solve problems on geometric sequences and series up to n terms.
Tell whether a sequence is arithmetic or geometric.
Solve problems on harmonic sequences and series up to n terms.
Find the sums of the first n natural numbers, their squares and their cubes.
Recognise an arithmetico-geometric sequence, find its general term and its sum to n terms and to infinity using sigma notation.
Identify the parts of a motor vehicle lease: down payment, insurance, charges and monthly instalments.
Solve vehicle leasing problems under different conditions.
Apply sequences and series to loans, interest, depreciation, investment and other real problems.
Describe an induction argument: base case, hypothesis and conclusion.
Prove statements, identities, divisibility and summation formulae by induction.
Judge and communicate a mathematical conclusion clearly in everyday settings.
State and use the binomial theorem to expand a binomial raised to a positive integer power.
Describe the binomial theorem as the expansion of binomial powers over natural numbers.
Read binomial coefficients from Pascal's triangle.
Expand with the binomial theorem and simplify the result.
Find approximate values using the binomial theorem.
Find remainders of large powers using the binomial theorem.
Use the binomial theorem for last digits, divisibility and comparing large numbers.
Apply induction and the binomial theorem to real problems such as puzzles and forecasting.
Divide a polynomial of degree up to 4 by a linear or quadratic polynomial to get quotient and remainder.
State and use the remainder theorem.
Use the factor theorem to factorise a cubic polynomial.
Apply the remainder and factor theorems to real problems such as regression and signal processing.
Recognise the rectangular coordinate system in space.
Define unit vectors i, j and k and write the components of a vector.
Find the magnitude of a vector.
Carry plane vector operations over to space.
Prove the commutative and associative laws, the null vector and the additive inverse for vector addition.
Explain the dot product and its geometric meaning.
Write the dot product in terms of components.
State the condition for two vectors to be orthogonal.
Use the dot product to find the angle between two vectors.
Find the projection of one vector along another.
Find the work done by a constant force along a given vector.
Solve everyday problems with the dot product.
Explain the cross product and its geometric meaning.
Use the cross product to find the angle between two vectors.
Solve everyday problems with the cross and dot products.
Describe the scalar triple product.
Write the scalar triple product as a determinant of components.
Prove the triple product identities and that dot and cross can be swapped.
Find the volume of a parallelepiped or tetrahedron from three vectors.
Define coplanar vectors and state the condition for three vectors to be coplanar.
Apply vectors in space to navigation, graphics and engineering problems.
Establish the fundamental law cos(a - b) = cos a cos b + sin a sin b.
Derive allied-angle ratios and double, half and triple angle identities from the fundamental law.
Change products of sines and cosines into sums or differences.
Find the domain and range of trigonometric functions.
Tell even and odd trigonometric functions apart and find their periods.
Find the maximum and minimum of functions such as a + b sin(c theta + d) and their reciprocals.
Graph and analyse sine, cosine and tangent to solve problems.
Explain the properties of the graphs of sine, cosine and tangent.
Apply trigonometric functions, identities, graphs and extreme values to real problems such as heights, navigation and periodic motion.
Explain and use the fundamental counting principle.
Explain and solve problems on permutations.
Explain and solve problems on combinations.
Apply permutations and combinations to real problems such as lotteries, DNA sequences and playlists.
